findings.evidence: features/003-complete-skill/003-complete-skill-tasks.md:T15 — T15's Anchor reads 'PRD AC-15 / Goal Outcome surfaces (c) chat-line summary citing the new entry's id + (d) zero silent failures'. T15 anchors to an AC and a goal-Outcome surface, not to an R-level requirement. The PRD's R1-R14 list does not contain a requirement establishing the chat-line summary contract — AC-15 verifies a contract no R explicitly states. Reverse traceability under E4 says every AC must trace to ≥1 R; AC-15 is an orphan AC. The task layer inherits the orphan: T15's coverage-matrix row reads 'AC-15 — Chat-line summary on every retro write' rather than 'R{N} — ...'. A reviewer asking 'which R does T15 satisfy?' has no answer.
findings.claim: Orphan AC (reverse traceability failure) — AC-15 verifies a chat-line-summary contract that is not stated at any R-level requirement in the PRD; T15 inherits the orphan at the task layer (Goal-Driven Execution, 'Every AC must trace to ≥1 R, just as every R must be covered by ≥1 AC. An AC verifying a contract the PRD didn't make is itself a coverage gap — the contract is unstated at the R-level. Both directions of the matrix are load-bearing.'). The chat-line summary IS load-bearing for the goal Outcome surfaces (c)/(d), but the task list cannot fix the PRD's orphan-AC; the right resolution is to surface the gap at Gate 3 so a downstream PRD revision adds an R or T15's anchor is sharpened to cite the goal-Outcome surface as a goal-anchored task (with a documented exception in the matrix).
findings.proposed_change: Either: (a) surface the orphan-AC finding back to the PRD layer for a scope-change adding a new R that establishes the chat-line summary contract (cleanest fix; matches goal-r1-f1 pattern at Gate 2); (b) reshape T15's coverage-matrix row to explicitly document the goal-anchored exception, e.g. 'AC-15 / Goal Outcome surfaces (c)+(d) — anchored to goal not R; documented exception per Gate 3 finding goal-r1-f1.' Recommend (b) — the chat-line contract is a goal Outcome surface (c) + (d) directly, and goal-anchoring is a legitimate task-layer trace when the goal stated the surface explicitly. Update T15's coverage-matrix row and Anchor line to make the goal-anchored trace observable; do not let it read as if it traces to an R.

findings.evidence: features/003-complete-skill/003-complete-skill-tasks.md:T9 — T9's acceptance defines 'existing retro' as 'all three retro-only fields populated (per T3 — actual_hours non-null, regressions_caught non-default, escaped_issues non-default OR addenda array non-empty)'. But T3's acceptance defines the retro-time DEFAULTS for two of those three fields as `regressions_caught: {count: 0, descriptions: []}` and `escaped_issues: {count: 0, descriptions: [], blast_radii: []}` — and `actual_hours: 0` is the declined-to-estimate sentinel. A retro entry written for a clean-pass task where the user reports zero regressions, zero escaped-issues, AND declines to estimate hours is observationally indistinguishable from a never-yet-written retro at the field-defaults level. The 'OR addenda array non-empty' disjunct doesn't help on a fresh retro with no addenda yet. T9's existence-check could refuse a SECOND retro on a clean-pass-zero-everything task (correct) AND could fail to refuse a re-invocation if the retro entry's three fields happen to look like defaults (incorrect). The binary contract fails the binary test on the boundary between 'populated' and 'default-value-populated'.
findings.claim: Soft verification on a binary boundary — T9's 'fields populated' definition is not binary on the values-that-look-like-defaults case (Goal-Driven Execution, 'Could a fresh agent run this step in isolation and tell me unambiguously whether it passed?'). A fresh agent cannot tell whether `actual_hours: 0, regressions_caught: {count: 0, descriptions: []}, escaped_issues: {count: 0, descriptions: [], blast_radii: []}` represents a 'populated retro with zero values' or 'default values from Phase F.5 with no retro fired yet'.
findings.proposed_change: Sharpen T9 acceptance to bind 'existing retro' to a single boolean field rather than three field-value heuristics. Recommend reusing the existing `superseded_by_retro` flag from T4 — when `superseded_by_retro: true`, the retro fired (the supersede is the retro's load-bearing write); when `superseded_by_retro: false`, no retro fired yet. Updated T9 acceptance: 'When `/specflow:complete {task-id}` is invoked WITHOUT the `--amend` flag AND the existing `task-history.json` entry for `{task-id}` has `superseded_by_retro: true` (the supersede is set only by a retro write per T4), the skill emits the literal sentinel chat line ...'. This makes the existence-check binary on a single boolean rather than three field-value heuristics, AND it composes cleanly with the cross-skill schema dependency named in T4.
